body.heading: Dependent Edits
body.html: Focused views assume the instruction carries every value an edit needs. Study U built the class where it doesn't: dependent edits ("set A's content to the same value as B's", "rename A to B's name") whose needed value is verified absent from the instruction AND from the rendered target-only view.

body.heading: Ninety Confident Fictions
body.html: That view failed all 90 cells across both models; and every single failure was a valid patch containing a silently invented value: zero refusals, zero invalid artifacts, 90/90 confident fictions that validate and apply.

body.heading: The One-Line Fix
body.html: The fix is one line: put both mentioned nodes in the focus ids. That scores a perfect 90/90; descriptively better than the whole tree, which fumbled 3 structure-reads at ~1000 nodes on sonnet; at ~1.7k median input tokens, 25× less than the full tree.

body.heading: Search Reads Values Badly
body.html: The shipped search recipe can self-serve reads at 82–84% (median 2–3 calls), significantly short of full-tree parity on gemini (p = 0.008) and weakest on value-copies (75%): search grounds targets at oracle level, but reading values is the application's job. Focus ids = every node the request mentions.

body.heading: The First Judge-Graded Study
body.html: The series' first judge-graded study, run under a pre-registered pairwise protocol: both judges (gpt-5.4 primary, haiku-4.5 sensitivity; neither an editor) first had to pass a 50-pair calibration gate with planted verdicts, identity probes, and length probes, and both aced it 50/50.

body.heading: The Task
body.html: The task: "rewrite this paragraph to focus on our central thesis," with the thesis planted in a mission node and the target paragraph deliberately assembled off-thesis. Five arms for where the goal lives.

body.heading: Blind Arms Polish Obliviously
body.html: Blind arms lost all 120 comparisons by obliviously polishing the off-topic paragraph; fluent, valid, useless.

body.heading: The Memo Carries the Goal
body.html: The T memo carried the goal at full parity with an explicit instruction (sonnet's memo arm actually won 10–2 under the primary judge).

body.heading: The Surprise That Failed the Gate
body.html: The surprise that failed the gate: models with the thesis-bearing node IN THE VIEW demonstrably read it (keyword coverage +0.75 vs +0.00 blind) yet lost 117/120; their rewrites orbit the topic where told-outright rewrites anchor the thesis. Study U's view fix moves data perfectly; it moves intent only partway.

body.heading: The Verdict
body.html: Judge agreement 83.3% (kappa 0.53); the keyword proxy ranks the arms identically. Guidance: put the nodes an edit must read in the view; put the goal in the instruction or memo, restated outright.

body.heading: From Oracle to Agent
body.html: Studies T and V validated the memo with oracle extraction: the harness knew what to record. What ships in production delegates that judgment to the agent via an update_session_notes tool and a prompt rule, with a 32-message history window also present; and within the window, callbacks succeed via history whether or not the agent records, so a lazy agent's empty memo is invisible until truncation.

body.heading: The Shipped Mechanism, Tested Verbatim
body.html: Study W tested the shipped mechanism verbatim (character-identity ports) on 36-step sessions that cross the window, with a mid-session retraction, on three models including claude-opus-4.8; the series' first data on the tier the production system runs.

body.heading: Both Gates Pass
body.html: Both gates passed. Pure agent extraction ties the oracle exactly (recall 36/36 per model, retractions 12/12, zero noise notes, one drop event in 72 sessions), the tool gets called ~4 times per session at exactly the declarative moments, and the laziness hypothesis is refuted: with history present the recording cadence is unchanged and post-truncation callbacks hold; opus a perfect 36/36, gemini 35/36, sonnet 31/36 (not significant, and not memo-explained: its memo was complete in every failing cell).

body.heading: Real Protection, Not Theater
body.html: The over-32-message protection is real protection, not theater. Filled dots: post-truncation callbacks; hollow: within-window.

body.heading: The Last Unmeasured Class
body.html: The last structurally unmeasured request class: follow-ups that point at the previous edit; "also set that same node's…", "apply the same change to X", "actually, undo that." Anaphora steps ran against skeleton views (an oracle-focused view would leak the answer), so the carrier under test had to supply the target, the key, AND the value.

body.heading: No Carrier, No Chance
body.html: Without one, no model resolves anything: 0 of 144 across sonnet, gemini, and opus, and every single failure was a valid, applied, silently guessed patch; the strongest silent-failure result in the series.

body.heading: The Echo Wins
body.html: Full history is near-ceiling (48/48, 48/48, 46/48). The winner is the cheapest carrier tested: a one-line last-edit echo the application appends automatically (set "key" from old to new on node), which ties history per model at about half the input cost and BEAT history outright on opus-4.8; 48/48 against history's 46/48, with the from/to format carrying every undo on every model.

body.heading: Fine Print
body.html: Fine print, disclosed: "apply the same change to X" strains compressed carriers model-dependently (sonnet 7/12 with the echo; window-2 leaks on repeat everywhere, significantly on gemini), one more entry in the carrier-advice-is-not-model-independent ledger.

body.heading: The Stack, Complete
body.html: The measured stateless session stack is now complete: fresh view per turn, two worked examples, the session-notes memo, and the last-edit echo.

body.heading: How People Actually Talk
body.html: Every declaration in Studies T, V, and W was announced formulaically ("For later reference: the codename is X"). Real users declare mid-sentence, bury rules inside other requests, and retract with "scratch that."

body.heading: Twin Sessions
body.html: Study Y isolated phrasing with twin sessions: identical trees, edits, schedules, chatter, and session ids, differing ONLY in declaration rider text; one twin formulaic, one casual from registered pools. Four chatter riders per session ("the client saw a screenshot and seemed happy") gave the noise metric real bait for the first time.

body.heading: Both Gates Pass
body.html: Both gates passed perfectly on all three models: zero discordant callback cells anywhere between casual and formulaic (every McNemar 0 to 0), recall 36 of 36 and casual retractions 12 of 12 in both stateless arms, and 432 chatter baits produced not one false memo note. Users need no announcement syntax, and the shipped record-only-declarations prompt rule is doing real discrimination work at zero false-positive cost.

body.heading: One Disclosed Whisper
body.html: One disclosed whisper: under the history window, recording cadence softens at the margin (3.8 to 3.9 calls per session vs a flat 4.0 stateless), consistent with Study W's redundancy finding and covered by in-window history. The formulaic arm doubled as a clean Study W replication under added chatter.

body.heading: Nobody Had Measured the Pack
body.html: Production doc editors ship a standing context block with every request; company facts, client records, a styleguide; and nobody had measured whether models actually use it.

body.heading: The Setup
body.html: Study Z planted machine-checkable obligations in twelve seeded org packs (~3.3k tokens: one target client, three same-schema distractors, governing rules rotated head/middle/tail among twelve styleguide rules) and raced three arms: the whole pack, an oracle-picked relevant slice, and the whole pack plus the applicable rules distilled into the session-notes memo.

body.heading: An Emphatic Answer
body.html: The core answer is emphatic: facts and rules were 216 of 216 per arm; 100% on every model in every arm; with zero cross-client contamination in 324 cells and no burial effect at any styleguide position.

body.heading: Slicing Buys Nothing
body.html: Slicing bought nothing on accuracy and forfeited prompt caching (the per-request slice never got a single cache read; the whole pack under the shipped cached-system layout read 64–68% of input from cache, cutting effective input cost 25–43%).

body.heading: The Accidental Conflict
body.html: The finding lives in a conflict we registered by accident: a contact-format rule written with "always" against an instruction clause asking for a product mention. Every model resolved it cleanly into one of two readings; satisfy both, or obey the format literally; with zero violations. Our first read of the split (strictness scales with capability) was REFUTED by its own pre-registered confirmation study a day later: see Study AA below.

body.heading: What Stands from Z
body.html: What stands from Z: distilling the rules into the memo did not change competence; it changed which reading wins (sonnet 2/12 → 11/12 satisfying both, p = 0.004). Audit your styleguide for "always" and "exactly": the failure mode of a conflicted spec is disciplined obedience to the rule you forgot you wrote.

body.heading: The Setup
body.html: Study Z’s spec-conflict split was an accident with one conflict shape, so Study AA measured it on purpose: three registered conflict kinds (rule vs instruction, an explicit user countermand of a rule, rule vs rule), four arms (base, a priority meta-rule, soft “generally prefer” phrasing, rules restated in the memo tail), 432 cells.

body.heading: The Prediction, Inverted
body.html: The confirmation gate predicted opus most literal and measured it LEAST literal; zero strict readings in 24 base cells against sonnet’s 10 and gemini’s 7, significant in the opposite direction (p = 0.016); and the same conflicted template that split opus 6/6 under Z’s three-rule packs read both-obligations 12/12 under AA’s four-rule packs: which reading wins is composition-sensitive, not a model constant.

body.heading: Three Interventions, One That Works
body.html: The interventions: the priority meta-rule (“the user’s request takes precedence”) moved nothing significantly on any model; softening “always” to “we generally prefer” collapsed literal readings (sonnet 10/24 → 2/24, gemini 7/24 → 0/24); the cheapest fix that works; and memo steering replicated Study Z to the digit (sonnet 2/12 → 11/12, p = 0.004) while revealing a footgun: with a rule restated in the memo, opus enforced the ™ mark against the user’s explicit “written plain, no trademark symbol” 12 of 12 times (without the memo, all 36 base cells honored the countermand). Rule-vs-rule conflicts resolved by specificity, not styleguide position.

body.heading: Study AB Closes the Footgun
body.html: The footgun is CLOSED, measured (Study AB, 144 cells): a one-sentence precedence clause inside the memo block; the production system’s shipped mitigation, tested verbatim; restored every trampled countermand (opus 0/12 → 12/12, p = 0.0005; sonnet 3/12 → 11/12) at zero cost to the memo’s steering benefit (satisfy-both stayed 12/12 everywhere), with the injury first replicated to the digit in the control arm.
The placement lesson: the same sentence class buried in the styleguide moved nothing; precedence language works at the point of injury, adjacent to the notes it governs.

body.heading: The Bottom Line
body.html: Across 900 conflicted cells in Z, AA, and AB: zero violations, zero contamination; models resolve conflicted specs; the conflict itself is the authoring hazard.

studies.title: The model always knew what it couldn’t see
studies.indexLine: Twenty-eight studies of silent failure (90/90 invented values in U, 144/144 silent guesses in X, 120/120 oblivious polishes in V, zero clarifying questions anywhere) never once OFFERED the model a way out.

body.heading: No Way Out, by Design
body.html: Twenty-eight studies of silent failure (90/90 invented values in U, 144/144 silent guesses in X, 120/120 oblivious polishes in V, zero clarifying questions anywhere) never once OFFERED the model a way out.

body.heading: Two Hatches, One Control
body.html: Study AC did, on Study U’s unit-validated construction: the needed value provably absent from the target-only view, provably present in the solvable twin. Two registered hatches; a one-sentence NEED-INFO prompt rule, and an ask_user tool; against a no-hatch control, 810 cells.

body.heading: The Flip
body.html: The control replicated U exactly: 135/135 silent wrong patches. Both hatches flipped it completely: 270/270 asks on unsolvable cells, ZERO false asks and untouched solve rates on the 270 solvable twins, and every single ask named the exact missing node and attribute ("What is the content attribute value of the text-atom with id n219?").

body.heading: Obedience, Not Blindness
body.html: The mechanisms were indistinguishable, so the one-sentence version is the whole result. The reframe: the models always saw the gap precisely; they guessed because the protocol demanded a patch and nothing said asking was allowed; obedience, not blindness.

body.heading: The Guidance
body.html: Guidance: ship an ask path (one sentence; wire it to a real reply mechanism), keep the context contracts (they make the question unnecessary; the hatch makes residual failures visible), and mind the disclosed caveat: this was measured at a validated hard boundary, not on merely-vague requests; calibration on fuzzy ambiguity is the follow-up. The follow-up is now measured: see the Study AE section below.

Study Q had already shown that serializer advice inverts between models, so nothing could be assumed.

body.heading: Every Gate Passes
body.html: Study AD re-ran the stack on opus with corpora, prompts, and graders reused verbatim: 1,160 cells, gates anchored to the weakest previously passing tier. Every gate passed, mostly at or above the top of the prior bands.

body.heading: The Numbers
body.html: The anchored-patch dialect scored 194/200 on the main corpus (the best condition-F number ever measured, and every miss was a tree-reading count question rather than an editing failure), HTML focused views swept 90/90 across 300 to 1000 nodes, search grounding landed exactly on sonnet's oracle bound (43/45, median one call), and all session policies were perfect.

body.heading: The Ablation Surprise
body.html: The surprise is the ablation: bare stateless sessions, no history and no worked examples, also scored 240/240 steps with 20/20 intact end states. The examples block that rescued sonnet (13/20 without it) is not load-bearing on the frontier tier; it is cheap insurance for every tier below it, and it stays shipped.

body.heading: Fan-Out Remains the Boundary
body.html: Fan-out remains the honest boundary, now with a third mitigation profile: opus raised the floor to 80 to 89% but still left a third of the 7-plus-target view tasks partially covered, so the app-side decomposition fence stands unchanged at every tier.

studies.title: Only the frontier knows when a question is the right answer
studies.eyebrow: Study AE · hatch calibration + the resume loop
studies.indexLine: Study AC left two fears on the record: that the escape hatch would tax clear requests with unnecessary questions, and that an ask might be a dead end.

body.heading: Two Fears on the Record
body.html: Study AC left two fears on the record: that the escape hatch would tax clear requests with unnecessary questions, and that an ask might be a dead end. Study AE measured both on a five-level ambiguity ladder (precise, indirect-but-unique, discretionary, ambiguous-referent, missing-info; every level's defining property unit-validated) with the shipped NEED-INFO sentence frozen verbatim, plus 135 resume cells where the harness answers the model's question in plain text.

body.heading: Both Fears Refuted
body.html: Both fears refuted at ceiling: zero false asks in 90 clear-request cells with solve rates identical to the no-hatch control, models edit "make it punchier" rather than interrogating the user about wording, and the ask-answer-patch loop closed 135 of 135 with zero re-asks and zero wrong integrations. An ask is a reliable two-turn solve, so reply paths can ship with confidence.

body.heading: The Failure Is the Finding
body.html: The gate still fails, and the failure is the finding: when a singular request matches exactly TWO visible nodes, opus-4.8 asks 15/15 and names both candidate ids every time, while sonnet and gemini ask 1/15 each even with the hatch present. They resolve the ambiguity unilaterally instead, in different ways: sonnet edits BOTH matches, gemini silently picks one.

body.heading: The Mechanism Is Textual
body.html: The mechanism is textual: the registered sentence covers information that is "not visible in the view," and an ambiguous referent is entirely visible. The frontier tier generalized the rule's intent; the mid tiers applied its letter, the same literalism profile Study AA measured on conflicting specs.

body.heading: The Guidance
body.html: Guidance: on the frontier tier the hatch now covers absence AND ambiguity; below it, app-side disambiguation (unique references, deterministic enumeration, selection grounding) remains the only defense, and the obvious multiplicity amendment to the hatch sentence stays unshipped until a registered test passes it.

studies.title: Saying the goal out loud doesn't make it yours
studies.indexLine: One clause in the shipped session-notes rule had been inferred rather than measured: restate a goal from the memo in your own words before a goal-directed rewrite.

figure.title: Judged Comparisons for Restate Arms vs. the Explicit-Goal Control

body.heading: An Inferred Clause
body.html: One clause in the shipped session-notes rule had been inferred rather than measured: restate a goal from the memo in your own words before a goal-directed rewrite. The hope was that forced verbalization would also rescue Study V's sharpest loss, where a model shown the node its goal lives in reads it and still writes measurably less focused prose (117 of 120 judged losses).

body.heading: The Protocol
body.html: Study AF measured the clause with Study V's full protocol: both judges re-passed their 50-pair calibration gate before any verdict, 270 contemporaneous edits (all mechanically valid), each restate arm judged against a same-batch explicit-goal control in both presentation orders.

body.heading: Dead Without a Single Win
body.html: The view-side hope is dead, without a single win: 0 wins, 79 losses, 11 ties pooled across three editors including opus.

body.heading: Compliance Was Perfect
body.html: And the failure is not disobedience. GOAL-line compliance was 30 of 30 in every cell: every model read the mission node, restated the thesis accurately in its own words, and then wrote the off-goal paragraph anyway. Verbalization is not the active ingredient; where the goal comes from is.

body.heading: On the Memo Path
body.html: On the memo path the clause measured neutral under the registered primary judge (parity on all three editors) with a disclosed sensitivity dissent toward mild harm (gemini 1 win to 13 losses, opus 5 to 15 under the second judge), and where Study V's bare memo had beaten the control outright on sonnet, memo-plus-restate merely ties.

body.heading: The Recommendation
body.html: The benchmark's recommendation: remove the clause. The memo itself keeps its goal-carriage parity, contemporaneously replicated here; the ceremony on top of it does nothing measurable. Views carry values, memos carry goals, and no prompt ritual converts one into the other.

related.title: Repeating the Goal Doesn't Make It Yours

studies.title: Perfect to the cap. At the cap, the goals die first.
studies.indexLine: Every study that shipped the session-notes memo measured it at three to six notes; the shipped implementation caps it at twenty, with a normalize step that silently drops the excess.

figure.title: Memo-Update Integrity Below and at the Twenty-Note Cap, by Model

table.summary: Read-side results and the cap-edge taxonomy

body.heading: Filling the Memo Up
body.html: Every study that shipped the session-notes memo measured it at three to six notes; the shipped implementation caps it at twenty, with a normalize step that silently drops the excess. Study AH filled it up.

body.heading: Flawless Below the Cap
body.html: Below the cap the memo is flawless at scale: recall of any note from a FULL twenty-note memo scored 15 of 15 per model at every position (no burial: first, middle, and last notes all perfect), unprompted rule application from a twelve-rule memo was 15 of 15 per model with zero cross-note contamination, and the agent's full-replace update was lossless wherever the update fit, 60 of 60 clean at ten and nineteen notes with the requested edit landing 90 of 90 alongside.

body.heading: The Twenty-First Declaration
body.html: Then a twenty-first declaration arrived at a full memo, and a note died in all 30 cells, silently. The victim was a goal note every single time, on every model.

body.heading: The Mechanism Is Structural
body.html: The mechanism is structural: the block renders facts, then rules, then goals, so goals are always the tail of the list, and both loss modes eat the tail: opus over-sent twenty-one notes all ten times and let the shipped clamp keep the first twenty; gemini and sonnet usually pruned a goal themselves.

body.heading: The Sharpest Possible Ordering
body.html: Study V measured goals as the one thing only the memo can carry, which makes this the sharpest possible failure ordering: at capacity, the memo sacrifices its most irreplaceable cargo first, with no error and, in the over-cap cases, no model decision at all.

body.heading: The Fix, Filed
body.html: The fix is application-side and filed: evict the oldest fact deterministically instead of clamping, never the goals tail, or surface memo-full to the user; prompt-side mitigations stay unshipped until measured. Below the edge, note-count is a provably safe budget.

studies.indexLine: Study AE left an obvious fix on the table: the shipped ask sentence covers what the model cannot see, so ambiguous references (visible, but two of them) slipped through on the mid tiers.

body.heading: The Obvious Fix
body.html: Study AE left an obvious fix on the table: the shipped ask sentence covers what the model cannot see, so ambiguous references (visible, but two of them) slipped through on the mid tiers. One added sentence covering requests that match more than one node looks like it must work, and this series has now caught two obvious-looking clauses doing nothing (the priority meta-rule in AA, the restate ceremony in AF), so the clause was measured before anyone shipped it: amended sentence versus the shipped one, re-run contemporaneously, across the full five-level ladder on three models.

body.heading: A Three-Way Split
body.html: The results split three ways. Sonnet is completely rescued: 3 of 15 asks became 15 of 15, every ask naming both candidate ids, with its silent edit-both habit gone. Gemini improved enormously, 0 of 15 to 11 of 15, but stopped one ask short of the registered detection bar, and its four residual failures all silently edited BOTH matches; the clause converted its coin-flips into asks or edit-boths, never back into correct restraint.

body.heading: Zero Tax Anywhere
body.html: And the clause taxed nothing anywhere: zero false asks in 90 clear-request cells, solve rates identical to control, hard boundaries undisturbed.

body.heading: The Cost Signal on Our Tier
body.html: The one cost signal lives on the tier we actually ship: opus, already perfect on ambiguity with the shipped sentence alone, started interrogating discretionary requests slightly more often under the amendment (asks on "make it punchier" cells rose from 2 of 15 to 5 of 15, not significant, but the only movement anywhere).

body.heading: The Verdict
body.html: So the registered gate fails by a single ask, and the practical verdict is sharper than a pass: the clause stays unshipped on frontier surfaces, where it buys nothing and whispers a cost; it is a large, free, but partial improvement for sub-frontier deployments; and app-side disambiguation remains the actual contract at every tier. Knowing when a question is the right answer keeps measuring as a capability that prompting approaches but does not close.

studies.title: The discourse gap closes on every tier; the visibility clause bites
studies.indexLine: One border of the ask-path map was never tested: Study X's discourse construction, where "undo that" against a carrier-less editor failed 0 of 144 with every failure a valid silent guess.

figure.title: Anaphora Outcomes by Escape-Hatch Arm and Model

body.heading: The Untested Border
body.html: One border of the ask-path map was never tested: Study X's discourse construction, where "undo that" against a carrier-less editor failed 0 of 144 with every failure a valid silent guess. The shipped ask sentence arguably covers it (a dangling referent is "not stated in the request"), so Study AG pointed the sentence at it: the carrier-less control, the control plus the shipped hatch, and the last-edit echo plus the hatch, across three models and 1,296 session steps.

body.heading: The Hatch Covers Discourse
body.html: The control replicated Study X to the digit. With the hatch, 138 of 144 silent guesses became questions, on every tier, and the asks show genuine recognition: "the request refers to 'that same node' from a prior instruction, but no such node is identified." Unlike ambiguity, which only the frontier tier notices, the discourse gap is letter-covered, and every model protects itself.

body.heading: The Tax Check Fails
body.html: Then the tax check failed on all three models, and the ask texts locate the mechanism precisely. With the echo supplying everything (the node id, the key, both values), models still asked on roughly 70% of anaphora cells, quoting the echo's own node id while refusing to proceed because that node "is not visible in the current view." An anchored patch needs only the id; the echo-without-hatch arm solved 48 of 48 under identical views.

body.heading: The Collision
body.html: This is the sentence's visibility clause colliding with skeleton views: the rule's letter says an unseen node warrants a question, so a fully specified, solvable edit becomes an interrogation. Ordinary steps in the same arm, whose views carry their targets, produced zero false asks in 288 cells.

body.heading: A Dependency, Sharpened
body.html: The guidance sharpens into a dependency: the hatch's zero tax is conditional on the focus-ids contract. Views that cover every mentioned node make the hatch free (measured three times now); outline-style protocols need target-carrying views, a self-serve view tool, or a re-scoped sentence that gets its own registered test first.

studies.title: The error message didn't matter
studies.eyebrow: Study AJ · the correction loop in isolation
studies.indexLine: Returning barkup's structured validation issues verbatim has been a design commitment in every arm of this series, the closing instruction of playbook guideline 01, and standing guidance in the production codebase, and i.

figure.title: Single-Shot Recovery by Feedback Arm and Model

table.summary: Recovery by arm, model, and corruption class

body.heading: A Commitment, Never Tested
body.html: Returning barkup's structured validation issues verbatim has been a design commitment in every arm of this series, the closing instruction of playbook guideline 01, and standing guidance in the production codebase, and it had never once been an experimental variable. Study AJ isolated it.

body.heading: Seeding the Loop
body.html: Because correction loops rarely trigger naturally (first-pass validity runs 84 to 99 percent), the loop was seeded: the known-correct patch for each task was corrupted by a registered operator (dangling ids, missing fields, malformed op kinds, bad placement anchors, unknown attributes), injected as the assistant's own prior turn, and confirmed to fail the shipped applier. Then exactly one feedback message went back, the only variable in the study: the full structured issues, bare issue codes, or nothing but "the anchored patch was invalid."

body.heading: The Result Is Parity
body.html: The result is parity. Opus recovered all 45 seeded failures in every arm, including from the bare sentence. Gemini scored an identical 42 of 45 in all three arms, and the three misses were the same cells every time, all in the one genuinely hard class (bad placement anchors); feedback quality changed nothing. Sonnet showed the only gradient, 45 to 44 to 42, not significant. Told a patch failed, models simply re-derive the correct edit from the task and the tree.

body.heading: One Nuance
body.html: One nuance runs in bare feedback's favor: its extra failures stayed visibly invalid rather than becoming plausible wrong fixes, so thin feedback does not even push toward silent errors.

body.heading: The Commitment Survives
body.html: The commitment survives with its rationale corrected: return the issues verbatim because it costs nothing and makes correction logs humane for the people debugging them, not because the loop depends on it. Disclosed caveats: seeded single-op corruptions are a constructed proxy for organic errors, and recovery was single-shot where the shipped loop allows three rounds, which would only narrow the gap further.

studies.title: The fix works where it can, and the frontier tier invented consolidation
studies.indexLine: Study AH found that a twenty-first declaration at the memo's full cap always kills a note, and the victim is always a goal.

figure.title: Goal Survival at the Memo Cap Edge, by Notice Arm and Model

table.summary: Goal survival at the cap edge by arm and model, pathway split, and pipeline guarantees

body.heading: The Fix That Shipped in a Day
body.html: Study AH found that a twenty-first declaration at the memo's full cap always kills a note, and the victim is always a goal. The production fix shipped within a day: an app-side eviction that runs before the truncation clamp and removes the oldest fact, then the oldest rule, and never a goal. But shipped-in-response-to-a-finding is not the same as measured, so Study AK applied the Study AB standard and re-ran the injury site with the tool handler as the only variable: the old silent clamp as a contemporaneous control, the eviction pipeline as the treatment.

body.heading: Three Results
body.html: Three results. First, the mechanical guarantee is perfect: in all 19 cells where a model sent an over-cap list, the pipeline admitted the new note, evicted only the oldest fact, and preserved every goal; zero contract violations. Second, the injury closes where the fix can reach it: goal survival at the cap edge went from 0 of 10 to 10 of 10 on opus and 0 to 6 of 10 on sonnet, while the control arm replicated the original injury almost to the digit, every victim still a goal. Third, no new damage: 60 of 60 updates below the cap passed through untouched.

body.heading: The Honest Boundary
body.html: The honest boundary was pre-registered and held exactly: the app cannot restore a note the model pruned before sending, and sonnet pruned 4 of 10 and gemini 6 of 10 cap-edge cells client-side, victims still goals; so below the frontier tier the guarantee covers the clamp pathway, not the model's own editing. A prompt-side fence for the prune pathway is filed for future measurement rather than shipped untested.

body.heading: Opus Invents Consolidation
body.html: And one unregistered moment worth the price of the study: told via the eviction notice that its update had cost a note, opus alone called the tool again with an eleven-note memo carrying all twenty-one facts, rules, and goals; it consolidated the memo's content into fewer sentences rather than accept a loss. The regression suite now guards the cap edge permanently: goal-safe eviction on the opus baseline, with a hard zero on goals evicted by the pipeline.

studies.title: The gate fails on a moved baseline; and unproven does not ship
studies.indexLine: Study AK left one pathway open: the app-side eviction cannot restore a note the model pruned before sending, and the mid tiers pruned goals client-side in 4 to 6 cells of ten.

body.heading: Measuring the Filed Fence
body.html: Study AK left one pathway open: the app-side eviction cannot restore a note the model pruned before sending, and the mid tiers pruned goals client-side in 4 to 6 cells of ten. AK's interpretation table filed the obvious candidate; one prompt sentence forbidding self-eviction ("never drop or trim an existing note to make room; the app decides evictions"); for measurement before shipping, and Study AL is that measurement, with the prompt rule as the only variable against the AK-eviction arm as its contemporaneous control.

body.heading: Right Where the Gates Cannot See
body.html: The fence looked right everywhere the gates could not see: pooled client prunes fell 5 to 1, goal survival rose to 10 of 10 on sonnet and 9 of 10 on gemini, all sixty under-cap updates stayed untouched, and the sentence cost nothing; the models were already sending complete lists; the fence changed which notes survived, not how many tokens moved.

body.heading: A Moved Baseline
body.html: But the pre-registered significance gate failed at p = .219, for a reason nobody registered: the control arm did not replicate its own three-day-old baseline. Sonnet's prune rate halved (4 of 10 to 2), gemini's too (6 of 10 to 3); same prompts, same corpus, same handler, temperature 0, the largest drift the series has caught between two measurements of the same construction. Against a five-prune pooled baseline, ten cells per tier cannot clear the bar.

body.heading: A Double-Edged Verdict
body.html: So the published verdict is deliberately double-edged: the registered reading ("the prune pathway is not instruction-closable") overstates what this run measured, and the honest reading; unproven, not disproven; still ships nothing, because unproven does not ship.

body.heading: What the Study Bought
body.html: What the study bought instead is sharper than a pass: the client-prune baseline itself is unstable week to week, which is the strongest argument yet for the filed alternative; an update shape that cannot express omission at all, so the guarantee stops depending on tier behavior holding still. Two smaller facts round it out: opus pruned for the first time in the series (a fact, not a goal; its goal safety stayed perfect), and consolidation-on-notice recurred, two sightings in two studies.

studies.title: The notice learned to ask for everything back
studies.indexLine: Twice in two studies; both times unregistered; opus answered an eviction notice by re-sending the memo compressed into fewer sentences carrying all twenty-one needles: told a note had died, the frontier tier invented l.

body.heading: The Anecdote
body.html: Twice in two studies; both times unregistered; opus answered an eviction notice by re-sending the memo compressed into fewer sentences carrying all twenty-one needles: told a note had died, the frontier tier invented lossless consolidation rather than accept the loss. Study AM measured the mechanism instead of admiring the anecdote.

body.heading: Choosing the Surface
body.html: The intervention surface was chosen by the series' own results: Study AL had just measured the agent-prompt-rule surface failing at the cap edge, and Study AB long ago measured the opposite surface; app-authored text at the point of injury; fixing what buried text could not. The eviction notice is exactly that surface, and it arrives attached to the event that makes it actionable. One sentence appended to it, the notice string the only variable, on a fresh seeded forty-task cap-edge corpus: the same facts, rules, and goals rewritten into fewer, denser notes; nothing needs to be lost.

body.heading: The Cleanest Pass in the Series
body.html: The result is the cleanest pass in the series: opus lossless recovery went from 3 of 40 spontaneous to 40 of 40 invited (p ≈ 3×10⁻¹¹), every planted needle surviving with kind fidelity 800/800; facts staying facts, rules staying rules, goals staying goals through the rewrite; zero degraded cells on any model, zero re-add churn, and about 570 extra output tokens for the recovery call.

body.heading: Shipped, Ungated
body.html: The sub-frontier tiers ignore the invitation entirely and harmlessly, so the sentence ships ungated. It shipped as v3.215.0 the same day. And the pass settles a design question beyond the cap: any future omission-proof update protocol now has a measured lossless behavior to beat, because merge-style semantics would structurally break the very consolidation this study just turned into a guarantee.

sections.title: Tool availability dissolves the visibility-clause tax

body.heading: The Open Exposure
body.html: Study AG left one exposure open: under outline views, the shipped ask rule converted fully specified edits into NEED-INFO about 70% of the time, because the target node was "not visible"; even with the last-edit echo supplying id, key, and both values. AN re-ran that construction with a get_template_view tool in hand, four arms, three models, 1,728 session steps.

body.heading: Availability Settles It
body.html: Availability alone settled it: anaphora success rose to 45–48/48 with essentially zero asks on every tier, models fetching at most one or two precise views or patching directly from the echo.

body.heading: Unsafe Below the Frontier
body.html: The registered "prefer fetching over asking" clause added nothing where tools existed; and the protection arm showed it is unsafe below the frontier: told to prefer tools, sonnet silently guessed half of its genuinely unanswerable cells and gemini burned 689 tool calls hunting the conversation-borne referent in the tree, while opus asked a perfect 48/48.

body.heading: The Fence
body.html: The clause stays unshipped; the fence is capability-shaped: give tool-bearing surfaces the ask rule freely, and never pair the rule with skeleton views on a surface that lacks the tools.

sections.title: The catalog read is the mechanism; warnings alone are not

body.heading: The Shipped Assumption
body.html: Replicator's CMS shipped a warn-only canonical-tag design on its agent publishing surface: a tags_list tool whose description says to copy names exactly, plus advisory lint with did-you-mean suggestions. AO measured the assumption across a 40-tag fixture catalog and 36 drafting tasks.

body.heading: Drift Is Structural
body.html: Without guidance, models NEVER matched exact canonical casing; 0/36 clean on all three tiers, so tag drift is structural, not sloppiness.

body.heading: The Tool Is the Mechanism
body.html: With the tool present, every model consulted it unprompted in 36/36 cells and landed on-catalog topics canonical on the FIRST attempt (Claude tiers 24/24, including every near-collision trap like llm→LLMs and frontend→Front-End); zero warning rounds were needed. Warnings without the tool recovered only 7–24/36; the lint can fix slug variants but cannot supply a catalog it never showed.

body.heading: One Honest Edge
body.html: One honest edge: given off-catalog topics, opus returned empty tag lists 12/12 rather than invent; defensible editorial caution the registered non-empty gate mis-scored, filed as a protocol lesson.

body.heading: The Design Stands
body.html: The shipped design stands: keep tool and lint together, no hard gating needed.

studies.title: The off-catalog fork: one sentence settles the foreign branch; the registration loses the adjacent one
studies.eyebrow: Study AP · the off-catalog fork · 576 cells
studies.indexLine: The frontier tier refuses to tag off-catalog topics unaided (12/12 empty, replicating AO); one sentence of tool-description guidance closes the sub-frontier gap on every tier; a guarded tag_create tool stays fully disciplined; the adjacent-class gate failed on solo-authored acceptable sets, and the AP′ re-score under an independently authored key passes.

table.summary: Foreign-branch closure by arm, adjacent readings, discipline checks, and the mint tier map

body.heading: The Fork AO Filed
body.html: Study AO ended with a protocol lesson: its non-empty "clean" definition mis-scored opus declining to tag off-catalog topics. AP registered that fork explicitly, splitting the old uncovered class into adjacent (a general canonical tag genuinely fits) and foreign (nothing does), and measured two candidate guidance sentences plus a guarded tag_create tool: 48 tasks, four arms, three models, 576 cells.

body.heading: The Foreign Branch Settles
body.html: Unaided, the frontier tier already refuses: opus returned empty tag lists on 12/12 wholly-foreign topics, replicating AO exactly, while gemini and sonnet stretched general canonical tags onto 5 of 12. Either guidance sentence closes that gap. The minimal empty text ("if no canonical tag genuinely fits, return an empty tags list") hit 12/12 on all three models, and its feared side effect, suppressing legitimate tags on adjacent topics, never appeared: zero empty adjacent cells in any arm on any model.

body.heading: The Tool Is Discipline-Safe, With a Tier Map
body.html: With a guarded tag_create in hand, no model produced a single invented tag in 144 tool-arm cells, and the server-side guard never fired: all 40 mints were well-formed, Title Case, and free of near-duplicates. Willingness split sharply by tier: gemini minted on every foreign topic (26 mints), sonnet 10, opus 4; the frontier tier prefers empty over minting. A sub-frontier agent grows the catalog by a dozen well-formed, unwanted tags per batch, so if the tool ships it ships tier-gated or with human approval on new tags.

body.heading: The Gate Failed on the Registration
body.html: The pre-registered gate failed by the letter: opus cleared 8/12 adjacent cells under the fork text against a ≥10 bar. The audit shows every failing cell was all-canonical; the misses are one or two extra, editorially arguable tags beyond the solo-authored acceptable sets (UX on a checkout-conversion piece, CSS on web components, Security on email deliverability). Under an anchored reading (all tags canonical, at least one from the registered set) adjacent scores 144/144 across every model and arm; that number is published as exploratory, not the registered definition. AO's lesson recurred one class over: acceptance criteria authored alone under-cover defensible editorial judgment.

body.heading: What Ships and What Waits
body.html: Nothing ships from a failed gate. Filed: AP′, which re-registers the adjacent conformance definition and re-scores the same frozen raw results with no new API spend; the guidance-text decision waits for it. The foreign branch does not wait: on registered gates, either sentence stops sub-frontier stretching onto wholly-foreign topics, and the frontier tier never needed the help.

body.heading: The AP′ Re-Score Closes It
body.html: AP′ ran the next day: three fresh-context editors (one of them a model not under test) re-authored the adjacent answer key from task text and catalog alone, with a mechanical 2-of-3 merge and a review that approved the key unchanged. Re-scored under the identical rule, the gate PASSES; opus cleared the fork-text bar at exactly 10/12 with the foreign branch unchanged at 12/12. The independent key absolved 28 of the 33 original misses and left 5 standing as genuine over-generalizations, so it was judgment, not generosity. The two guidance sentences tied under the new key, which makes the shorter empty text the ship candidate. The lesson is now process: acceptance sets are authored by independent passes, never by the analyst alone.
